title: GPU entitlement compact rollup — per-contract snapshot
content:
Purpose:
This compact rollup is a working snapshot (april 18, 2028) of per-contract dedicated GPU entitlements across regions. It's intended for quick runway checks, conflict detection, and handoff to capacity planning for Q3 ramp windows.

Key notes / assumptions (short):
- We treat a 'slot' as 1 x A100-80GB-equivalent. H100 slots are weighted 1.6x for throughput parity; L40 is 0.45x.
- Overhang buffer: 6% of total committed slots set aside for live failover (cannot be reallocated without exec approval).
- Burst policy: customers with burst addenda can exceed baseline up to 30% for up to 12 contiguous hours, subject to global headroom.
- Fairshare policy: when contention occurs, latency-sensitive tiers (enterprise-sla) get priority; midmarket reduced gracefully via queued preemption windows.

Summary table (compact):
Contract | Customer | Region affinity | SKU mix (slots) | Baseline slots | Burst addendum | Utilization (30d avg) | Ramp window
C-2147 | Veridian Labs | us-west1 / global fallback | 40 A100 + 8 H100 (weighted 52.8) | 52 | +30% | 78% | May 1 - Jun 30
C-3339 | Kyndra Health | eu-west1 | 24 H100 (weighted 38.4) | 39 | none | 64% | steady-state (no ramp)
C-4012 | NovaRetail | us-east1 / ap-southeast1 | 60 L40 + 12 A100 (weighted 39) | 39 | +15% | 87% | Jun 15 - Jul 15 (phased)
C-2981 | Orion Platform | us-west1 | 16 A100 | 16 | +30% | 55% | urgent: move 4 slots to us-east1 by 2028-05-05
C-4890 | Mercury Apps | ap-southeast1 | 10 H100 + 6 A100 (weighted 22) | 22 | none | 22% | Q4 planning

Notes on outliers:
- NovaRetail (C-4012) is the hottest ticket: current 30d utilization 87% on their weighted entitlement of 39 slots. They are scheduled for a phased ramp that will require temporary burst capacity in us-east1 and a short-term lift of overhang if demand persists. Recommend approving 6 additional temporary slots (H100 if available) and schedule a migration test of standing L40 workloads to reserved L40 pool.
- Veridian Labs burst clause has never been exercised; confirm legal signoff if we require burst enforcement (legal/CS flagged).

Regional capacity snapshot (global pool converted to A100-equivalents):
Region | Total equiv slots | Committed (baseline) | Committed + overhang | Free headroom
us-west1 | 1,140 | 820 | 888 | 252
eu-west1 | 780 | 460 | 488 | 292
us-east1 | 920 | 610 | 646 | 274
ap-southeast1 | 480 | 240 | 255 | 225
Notes: headroom computed after 6% overhang reserved. ap-southeast1 has the largest relative headroom vs committed (good candidate for temporary bursts).

Allocation rules applied in snapshot:
- Affinity honors regional preference where provided; fallback region is applied only when local headroom < 8% of requested entitlement for first 72 hours post-request.
- Cross-region replicas: for customers that requested geo-redundancy we reserve 20% of entitlement in the secondary region but mark as 'read only' for billing until activated.
- Migration reserve: when moving entitlements we only shift 70% immediately; 30% left for cutover and validation window.

Short action items (owner in parentheses):
- Approve temporary 6-slot H100 uplift for C-4012 (Ethan Morris / capacity-committee) — due 2028-04-21.
- Confirm Veridian legal burst activation clause (Priya Nair) — due 2028-04-22.
- Schedule migration test for Orion (C-2981) 4-slot movement to us-east1 (Marco Alvarez / runbooks) — target 2028-05-03.
- Create an automated alert: if utilization > 85% on weighted entitlement for 7 consecutive days, create an infra-incident and tag PM/SE (Talia Chen) — open ticket INFRA-2956.

Potential stress scenarios (quick):
- Scenario A (regional outage us-west1): triggers fallback for Veridian (40% of traffic) to us-east1 and ap-southeast1. Headroom check: us-east1 can accept up to 120 A100-eq before impacting current commitments; contingency ordering needed if sustained >48h.
- Scenario B (massive seasonal spike for NovaRetail): sustained 45% traffic increase over 14 days — would require converting 30% of on-demand pool into dedicated temporary reservations or enforcing customer-level throttles.

Audit and validation notes:
- This rollup reconciles against the canonical ledger (see linked Confluence) and the reservation DB snapshot taken 2028-04-17T23:00Z. Minor drift: two commitments in eu-west1 (C-3339) were under-counted by 3 H100-equivalents in previous export; corrected here.
- Billing flag: C-4890 has a pending invoice dispute for January credits; finance requested allocation freeze until resolved. Marked as "billing-frozen" in the ledger (does not change physical reservation but prevents auto-extend).

C-4012|NovaRetail|us-east1/ap-southeast1|L40:60,A100:12|baseline:39|burst:+15|util:87%|ramp:2028-06-15:2028-07-15
C-2981|Orion Platform|us-west1|A100:16|baseline:16|burst:+30|util:55%|action:move4->us-east1 by 2028-05-05
C-4890|Mercury Apps|ap-southeast1|H100:10,A100:6|baseline:22|burst:none|util:22%|plan:q4

If you want a full sheet export (per-slot rows, cost buckets, hourly run-rate), say "export detailed runway CSV" and I'll append the expanded table.

Historical versions & comments:

- 2028-04-12: applied H100 weighting update (1.55x -> 1.6x).
- 2028-04-17: corrected eu-west1 H100 undercount for C-3339 and adjusted headroom calculations.
